metadata.title: How science governs itself — and is governed
metadata.origin_rule: Selected field, technical, institutional or governance anchors. A proposal or first mapped framework is not necessarily the discovery or beginning of the field. Earlier anchors remain visible at the left boundary.
metadata.restriction_rule: Hatched strips mark documented restrictions affecting a specified subset. Their height is not a fraction of the field. No fading is used because slowdown magnitude has not been measured.
metadata.success_rule: Green marks show scientific or clinical milestones; they do not demonstrate policy effectiveness. Casgevy is a somatic treatment, not heritable editing.
metadata.failure_rule: Red marks identify documented ethical breaches or adverse events with alleged oversight failures. Exact attribution remains source-specific. Absence of a mark is not evidence of success.
metadata.ordering: Oldest selected field-origin anchors first. Ties, including the unresolved pre-1945 group, are ordered by first plotted event; this does not establish the relative age of those fields. c.1950 represents the 1950s, not an exact founding year.
metadata.coverage: Selected UK, US and international governance cases; not an exhaustive list. Includes treaties, WHO guidance, international professional and industry standards, and scientific agreements. Chinese and Japanese domestic law and standalone EU instruments are omitted. Global scientific milestones and relevant breaches of international norms remain context. Historical rules are not a statement of current law.
metadata.colour_rule: Red shows selected restrictions in at least one mapped setting, within the scope printed beside the lane. Stem-cell red concerns NIH hESC line eligibility; heritable-editing red concerns reproductive use. Other restrictions remain in the evidence table. Blue and green show selected frameworks, not complete worldwide coverage.
metadata.overview_rule: Selected major milestones and responses. Related implementation steps can share an overview label; the marker remains at the named final step. Separate events and source links remain in the evidence table.

lanes.name: Human-participant protections
lanes.origin: Research involving human participants predates 1945; origin unresolved

events.label: 1962 US drug-trial safeguards
events.detail: US drug-investigation protections; not all human-participant research.

events.label: 1966 US PHS review policy
events.detail: Institutional review requirement within PHS-funded research; not all studies worldwide.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 1972 Tuskegee exposed
events.detail: Marker dates public exposure, not the start of abuse. The study ran from 1932 to 1972.

events.label: 1979 Belmont
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2004 UK trial rules
events.detail: Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004, original version. Covers medicinal-product trials, including authorisation, ethics review and participant protection; not all human-participant research.

events.label: 2017 revisions published
events.detail: Common Rule revisions published 2017; general compliance date 21 January 2019. Publication is not commencement.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2019 Revised Common Rule compliance
events.detail: General compliance date 21 January 2019; distinct from 2017 publication and July 2018 effective date. Overview entry includes earlier related steps listed separately in the evidence table. Its marker remains at the stated final step; it is not a new shared event date.

grouped_context.label: 2017 revisions published
grouped_context.detail: Common Rule revisions published 2017; general compliance date 21 January 2019. Publication is not commencement.

events.label: 2026 UK trial reform effective
events.detail: 2025 clinical trial amendments implemented 28 April 2026.

lanes.case_detail: Combined Nuremberg, Helsinki, Tuskegee, National Research Act, Belmont, and Common Rule history. Research involving human participants includes more than clinical trials. These instruments differ in scope and legal authority.

lanes.name: Animal research / 3Rs and ASPA

events.label: 1959 3Rs
events.detail: Replacement, reduction, refinement: a framework for alternatives, not a single replacement technology.

lanes.case_detail: Professional replacement principles and UK statutory oversight. The 3Rs source dates the framework, not the beginning of animal research.

lanes.name: Biological weapons / BWC
lanes.origin: Activity predates 1960; not a new field

prior_governance.label: Geneva Protocol 1925
prior_governance.detail: Earlier prohibition on use in war; not an approval system for peaceful research.

lanes.name: Pathogen research and controls

events.label: Koch’s anthrax experiments · 1876
events.detail: Koch demonstrated the causal role of the anthrax bacterium in 1876. Selected experimental milestone, not the first pathogen research or first oversight. Selected RKI institutional history passage reviewed 6 November 2026; original 1876 paper not read.

events.label: 1974 CDC classification
events.detail: CDC hazard classification of etiologic agents, cited in BMBL history. Advisory biosafety classification; not select-agent security law.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 1975 DPAG established
events.detail: Dangerous Pathogens Advisory Group first met 14 November 1975 following Godber recommendations. Advisory assessment of dangerous-pathogen laboratories and precautions, alongside general workplace law.
events.selection_note: Overview: first meeting, not handbook publication.

events.label: 1976 DPAG precautions
events.detail: Official inquiry paragraph 162 records the October 1976 handbook and code of practice. Advisory safeguards, not a universal pathogen licensing law. Separate from the November 1975 first meeting.
events.selection_note: Evidence only: October 1976 handbook follows the November 1975 first meeting.

events.label: 1997 Select-agent transfer rules effective
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2003 Possession rules effective
events.detail: Overview entry includes earlier related steps listed separately in the evidence table. Its marker remains at the stated final step; it is not a new shared event date.

events.label: 2012 federal review
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2015 Institutional DURC implemented
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2025 NIH DGOF restrictions
events.detail: June 18: specified foreign projects terminated, other covered projects suspended; not all pathogen research.

events.label: 2026 High-risk policy released
events.detail: 28 July release notice; underlying policy dated 20 July. Identified potential DGOF work remains paused pending implementation requirements.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 1975 Godber report published
events.detail: Government published the report and accepted its general recommendations. A central advisory group and voluntary system were being established. Existing workplace duties and local precautions preceded this framework. Ministerial statement read; full Godber report not read.

restrictions.label: 2012–13 selected H5N1 work
restrictions.detail: Voluntary pause on specified H5N1 research; not all influenza research.

restrictions.label: 2014–17 selected US-funded work
restrictions.detail: US funding pause for defined gain-of-function work. Historical interval, not a statement of current policy.

restrictions.label: 2025–chart end NIH-defined DGOF pause
restrictions.detail: Only covered NIH-supported activities; no verified lifting date. Shown to chart endpoint, not a claim that the restriction ends there.

lanes.case_detail: US select-agent controls and US research/funding oversight, alongside the international H5N1 voluntary pause. These controls have different scopes and do not apply to every pathogen study.

lanes.name: Life sciences / journal safeguards

events.label: 2003 Joint editors’ statement / PNAS policy
events.detail: Joint Journal Editors and Authors Group statement published in PNAS 100:1464, alongside Nicholas Cozzarelli’s PNAS-specific policy editorial on p.1463 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC149849/). Parallel statements appeared in other journals. This is selected professional self-regulation, not a universal publishing law or verified compliance by every journal.

lanes.case_detail: Distinguishes the joint editors’ statement from the accompanying PNAS-specific publication policy. Same February 2003 episode, not a PNAS-only international standard.

lanes.name: IVF / UK fertility rules

events.label: Rabbit IVF · 1959
events.detail: Min Chueh Chang, Fertilization of rabbit ova in vitro, published 8 August 1959. Selected mammalian IVF milestone, not the beginning of IVF research. Publication metadata and selected Nobel scientific-background passages reviewed 6 November 2026; original article not read in full.

events.label: 1969 human IVF
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 1984 Warnock
events.detail: UK governance framework covering fertility treatment and embryo research; shown here in the fertility-treatment context.

events.label: 1985 Voluntary licensing
events.detail: Interim voluntary licensing authority established; year-only anchor.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 1990 HFE Act
events.detail: UK governance framework covering fertility treatment and embryo research; shown here in the fertility-treatment context.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 1991 HFEA licensing begins
events.detail: Statutory licensing from 1 August 1991; distinct from the 1990 Act. Overview entry includes earlier related steps listed separately in the evidence table. Its marker remains at the stated final step; it is not a new shared event date.

grouped_context.label: 1985 Voluntary licensing
grouped_context.detail: Interim voluntary licensing authority established; year-only anchor.

grouped_context.label: 1990 HFE Act
grouped_context.detail: UK governance framework covering fertility treatment and embryo research; shown here in the fertility-treatment context.

lanes.case_detail: Fertility treatment and its UK governance: human IVF, first IVF birth, Warnock, and the HFE Act. The UK framework also governs embryo research; this lane focuses on fertility treatment. iPSCs are not shown as an alternative to IVF.

lanes.name: Laboratory biosafety
lanes.origin: 1955 biological safety conferences; a professional milestone, not the first safety practice

events.label: 1975 GB workplace duties
events.detail: Parliament records laboratory workers brought under health and safety legislation in April 1975. General workplace duties in Great Britain, not a biosafety-specific licensing system; Crown enforcement qualifications apply.

events.label: 1984 CDC/NIH BMBL
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 1995 COSHH bio-agent duties
events.detail: COSHH Regulations 1994 commenced 16 January 1995. Included specific biological-agent controls. HSE confirms the first-use notification duty began on this date. Great Britain; not an assertion that no earlier duties existed.

events.label: 2014 CDC potential anthrax exposure
events.detail: Potential exposure and documented laboratory safety failures. CDC reported no staff believed ill with anthrax as of 10 July 2014. The affected laboratory was closed for select-agent work pending corrective actions; no end date is plotted because it has not been verified.

events.label: CDC transfer moratorium
events.detail: Implemented moratorium on transfers of biological materials from CDC BSL-3/4 facilities after anthrax and H5N1 incidents. Resumption required lab-by-lab review; first specified TB-lab transfers resumed on 24 July. Broader improvements included initiated and planned actions. Not a new UK law.

events.label: 2020 WHO revision
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

lanes.case_detail: Mixed legal and advisory governance. Great Britain workplace protection from April 1975 and specific COSHH biological-agent requirements from 16 January 1995 coexist with WHO and CDC/NIH guidance. These are selected anchors, not the origin of laboratory biosafety worldwide.

events.label: 2010 HHS screening guidance
events.detail: HHS Screening Framework Guidance for Providers of Synthetic Double-Stranded DNA, effective 13 October 2010. Recommended baseline screening standards, distinct from the 2009 industry protocol and later procurement funding conditions. Original notice metadata and selected indexed passages reviewed 6 November 2026; full guidance not read in this pass.

events.label: 2024 UK screening guidance
events.detail: 8 October UK nonbinding guidance; controlled sequences can also engage existing law.

events.label: 2025 NIH procurement conditions
events.detail: NIH-funded procurement requirement effective 26 April 2025. Not a universal synthesis law; later federal revisions need separate mapping.

lanes.name: Gene therapy

events.label: 1972 Gene-therapy proposal
events.detail: Friedmann and Roblin proposed gene therapy for human genetic disease. Conceptual starting milestone, not an experimental discovery or treatment.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 1990 First gene-therapy trial
events.detail: Therapeutic gene-transfer trial began 14 September 1990. Earlier gene-marking experiments and 1972 proposals are distinct.

events.label: 1999 Gelsinger death
events.detail: Failure signal: fatal adverse event and later government allegations of oversight and reporting failures. The 2005 civil settlement contained no admission of those allegations.

events.label: 2008 EU advanced-therapy rules apply
events.detail: Regulation (EC) No 1394/2007, adopted 13 November 2007, applies from 30 December 2008. Covers advanced therapy medicinal products, including gene therapies; this marker records application, not adoption or a blanket authorisation for experiments. UK was then an EU member; no unchanged UK regime through 2026 is implied. Selected official legislative and European Commission passages reviewed 6 November 2026; full regulation not read in this pass.

events.label: 2017 Luxturna approved [US]
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2023 Casgevy authorised
events.detail: UK MHRA authorisation of a somatic CRISPR gene therapy in November 2023. This is medicinal-product oversight, not heritable-editing self-regulation.

restrictions.label: 2005–10 sponsor restriction
restrictions.detail: Five-year ban on James Wilson sponsoring FDA-regulated clinical trials. Applies to one investigator, not the whole gene-therapy field.

lanes.case_detail: Gene-therapy oversight, adverse events and authorised somatic treatments, including Casgevy.

lanes.name: Modified organisms / Cartagena

events.label: 1972 Recombinant DNA
events.detail: Selected technical landmark in genetic engineering; not the first modification of organisms by breeding or every biotechnology.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2003 entered into force
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2004 UK becomes party
events.detail: UK party from 17 February 2004. US not a party. Protocol concerns transboundary movement of living modified organisms, with specified scope/exemptions. Overview entry includes earlier related steps listed separately in the evidence table. Its marker remains at the stated final step; it is not a new shared event date.

lanes.case_detail: Cartagena Protocol: transboundary living modified organisms; blue from 2003 refers to Protocol parties, not a universal GMO approval framework. UK party from 2004; US not a party.

lanes.name: Engineered gene drives / guidance
lanes.origin: 2003 engineering proposal anchor; natural drives are older

events.label: 2014 GB contained-use law
events.detail: In force 1 October 2014; applicable contained GMO work, including qualifying engineered-drive organisms. Earlier 2000 rules not yet mapped.

events.label: 2016 National Academies recommendations
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2021 WHO testing guidance
events.detail: WHO second-edition framework for testing genetically modified mosquitoes, including gene-drive technologies. International guidance, not a binding global law; narrower than all gene-drive uses.

lanes.case_detail: Scope is proposed engineered drives, not the origin of natural gene drive. The 2016 report recommends phased testing; it is not a law or a moratorium.

lanes.name: AI laboratories / biosecurity

events.label: 2004 Robot scientist
events.detail: Selected robot-scientist demonstration; earlier laboratory automation exists.

events.label: 2009 Adam
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

lanes.case_detail: A technology-and-governance case. WHO guidance covers AI among emerging technologies. AIBL is a programme announcement, not a demonstrated safety outcome or a regulatory statute.

events.label: 2012 Programmable CRISPR
events.detail: Programmable CRISPR-Cas9 cleavage platform; not a heritable clinical treatment.

events.label: 2016 UK embryo-editing licence
events.detail: HFEA approval for embryo research; not permission for reproductive use or transfer to a woman.

events.label: 2018 Edited births reported
events.detail: Reported heritable editing violated international norms, according to the summit statement. Marker does not establish failure of every applicable policy.

events.label: 2018 summit
events.detail: Nonbinding organising-committee statement following the claim discussed at the summit. Condemns the experiment and calls for standards; does not itself change UK law.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

lanes.name: Human embryo models / code

events.label: 2021 ISSCR model guidance
events.detail: 2021 ISSCR guidance includes stem-cell-based embryo models. Nonbinding guidelines.

events.label: 2025 ISSCR model update
events.detail: August 2025 version 1.2 update focused on stem-cell-based embryo models.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

lanes.case_detail: The 2014 model is a precursor milestone, not an integrated embryo. The 2024 UK code is voluntary guidance and not the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Act.

lanes.name: Stem-cell research

events.label: 1991 UK embryo licensing
events.detail: Embryo-research licensing predates human ESC derivation. 2001 expanded research purposes, not the first licence regime.

events.label: 2001 UK research purposes expanded
events.detail: HFE (Research Purposes) Regulations 2001 expanded purposes for licensed embryo research, including serious disease and treatment research. Effective 31 January 2001; historical original version.

events.label: 2006 mouse iPSCs
events.detail: Induced pluripotent stem cells generated by reprogramming mouse cells. Early methods carry technical and safety limitations.
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2006 ISSCR guidelines
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: 2007 human iPSCs
events.detail: Human somatic-cell reprogramming supplies pluripotent cells without deriving a new embryonic stem-cell line from an embryo. It can reduce embryo use for some questions, but is not a replacement for all embryo research or proof of universal clinical safety. Non-embryonic reprogramming alternative; the hESC line-eligibility restriction does not apply to iPSCs as such.

events.label: 2021 revision
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

events.label: Registry pause [US]
events.detail: Pause on review/approval of new hESC registry lines; existing registered lines remain usable. Embryo derivation funding remains prohibited.

restrictions.label: 2001–09 US federal funding limit
restrictions.detail: Eligibility restriction on US federal support for human embryonic stem-cell research, not a worldwide prohibition. Other restrictions were not all removed in 2009.

lanes.case_detail: Combined cases: Stem-cell research / embryos and iPSCs; Stem cells / ISSCR guidelines. Embryo-derived human pluripotent stem-cell research, US funding restrictions, and reprogrammed-cell alternatives. Mouse iPSCs in 2006 precede human iPSCs in 2007. These alternatives apply to some stem-cell research questions, not to replacing IVF treatment. International professional guidance, distinct from national law. Human embryonic stem cells are the selected scope; stem-cell research has earlier roots.

lanes.name: Engineered organisms
lanes.origin: 1972 recombinant DNA: selected technical landmark, not all organism modification

events.label: 1972 Recombinant DNA
events.detail: Technical landmark associated with recombinant-DNA governance.

events.label: 1975 Asilomar
events.detail: Conference on recombinant-DNA research and containment precautions. Its recommendations were distinct from the later NIH funding conditions; the meeting itself did not create a worldwide legal regime.

events.label: 2010 commission report
events.selection_note: Evidence only; omitted from the overview for readability.

restrictions.label: 1974–75 selective pause
restrictions.detail: Voluntary pause on selected experiments. Asilomar did not remove all restrictions.

lanes.case_detail: Combined cases: Synthetic biology / US commission; Recombinant DNA / Asilomar. A synthetic genome controlled a recipient bacterial cell; this was not life built entirely from nonliving components. The commission report is advice.
